correctness.rationale: Choose d=a+b and V=U⊕<d>, a=(c,0), b=(c,1). Direct substitution gives (u,t)∘(v,s)=(v,s+1_{u+v=c}+1_{u=c}). The left-translation group independently flips all Q−1 nonzero U-fibres, while the two points above 0 are singleton orbits. Any automorphism normalizes these intrinsically defined fibres and has (phi(u),t+eta(u)) with phi(0)=0. Conjugating translations forces phi(u+c)=phi(u)+c, and substitution proves sufficiency. The centralizer on Q/2 two-cycles fixes {0,c}, yielding C2 wr S_{Q/2−1}; arbitrary bit functions eta give 2^(Q−1) pointed and 2^Q unpointed factors. Linear phi fixing c and linear eta yield 2^(2r−3)|GL_(r−2)(2)|. Explicit socle equation gives |Soc|=4 for r=2 and 2 otherwise; quotient is trivial, so level 1/2. Independently enumerated all permutations at r=2,3 and obtained pointed/unpointed counts (2,4),(16,32). Larger-r results rest on the normalizer proof, not enumeration.
residual_risks: The independently enumerated automorphism groups are only ranks r=2 and 3; rank 4/5 are corroborated by source script, not independent permutation exhaustion.
The definition of socle is the specified tau-group additive socle, not an arbitrary other cycle-set socle convention.
